title: SME Knowledge Review
markdown:
Knowledge that flows into retrieval passes through a subject-matter-expert (SME) review gate before it can influence the Executive. The queue and its decisions live in `openexecutive.knowledge.review_store.ReviewStore`, which shares the same `./episodic_memory.db` SQLite database as episodic memory.

Items enter the queue in a pending state. An SME then resolves each one:

- **Pending** — awaiting an SME decision. The Executive never sees pending items; they are excluded from every retrieval until resolved.
- **Rejected** — filtered out of every retrieval. A rejected item can never surface in a specialist's context.
- **Approved** — eligible for retrieval, and can be promoted in priority so it ranks ahead of unprioritized material.

### Effect on retrieval

The gate is a filter layered on top of the normal RAG path: a chunk only reaches a specialist if it is approved (or never required review). Rejection is durable and global — it removes the item from all future queries rather than just down-ranking it. Approval with priority promotion lets an SME push vetted, high-value knowledge to the top of the retrieved set. The net effect is that the curated knowledge the Executive reasons over is exactly the set an SME has signed off on, with rejected material held back and pending material invisible.
